title: ‘838’ number plate, pool of blood, screams: Chilling video captures daylight murder
content: In a shocking act of violence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, bystanders witnessed a murder as Devesh Dixit was pursued and collided with a vehicle. His friend-turned-assailant, Pawan Parashar, went on to deliver a fatal blow using a stick and iron rod. The police arrived shortly after, and Parashar voluntarily surrendered later at the station. Investigations continue to reveal the motive behind this brutal attack.

title: Burnt body of Class 12 student found behind guard room at Delhi school
content: An 18-year-old girl was discovered burnt behind the guard room of a school in Krishna Nagar. Police received a call regarding the fire incident and promptly arrived at the scene. They conducted preliminary proceedings and collected materials from the spot, including the victim's school bag. A crime team thoroughly inspected the location to gather evidence for the ongoing investigation.

title: When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
content: Sonia Gandhi officially joined the social media platform X to share personal memories and insights. In her first post, she introduced her upcoming memoir titled Belonging: A Journey of Love. The memoir recounts her life experiences, including her first meeting with Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge. Scheduled for release on November 10, the book details her journey through love and loss.

title: Kentucky court rejects bid to use neighbour's driveway after land split
content: In a Kentucky court case, Charlie E. Stearns and Kathy Stearns faced a setback in their property dispute against neighbors John and Betty Warinner. The Stearnses asserted that their long-term use of a pathway should grant them an implied easement. However, the jury found alternative access routes viable, leading to the dismissal of their claim, a verdict affirmed by the appeals court, confirming that historical usage doesn’t automatically legitimize easements.

title: Tilak Varma breaks world record during India vs New Zealand 2nd T20I
content: Tilak Varma achieved a historic milestone by taking the most catches in T20 Internationals during 2026. His remarkable performance included two catches in the second T20I against New Zealand. Varma surpassed the previous record held by Danilson Hawoe with a total of 26 catches this year. India won the toss and opted to bowl, making two changes to their playing XI.

title: Megan Thee Stallion-backed project delivers over 2,200 care packs to Black girls
content: In January 2024, 12-year-old Mila Henry founded MH Boxes, aiming to support Black girls facing mental health challenges. With a $550 grant from the #BlackGirlJoyChallenge, she crafted care packages containing essential self-care items. To date, the initiative has successfully distributed over 3,300 boxes nationwide, striving to break the stigma surrounding mental health in the Black community.

title: New York court revives privacy claim over cameras filming family's backyard
content: A couple in New York found themselves entangled in a complex property disagreement with their neighbors regarding a disputed land boundary tied to a chain-link fence. This conflict escalated, resulting in claims of trespassing and invasion of privacy due to surveillance cameras. Although the court struggled to rule on the boundary dispute, it has permitted the couple's privacy claims to advance for further scrutiny.

title: As Tesla promotes product Musk predicted 80% of value will come from, costs jump
content: Elon Musk has announced the start of production for Tesla's humanoid robot, named Optimus, in Fremont, California. The production phase is still in its early stages and might experience challenges. Despite a decline in revenue from Tesla's solar and energy storage business, there is positive growth in its services sector. Musk estimates the company could manufacture 20,000 robots per week by the end of 2027.

title: Denied library entry as boy, he helped open one; graduates rose from 4 to 30
content: Faced with caste discrimination when trying to access a library, V Selvakumar took matters into his own hands by starting a project to create one in Semmadu village. The result? A remarkable leap in educational achievement, with graduates rising from four to thirty. The local community, including youth and officials, rallied to sustain the library, emphasizing the transformative power of equitable educational access.

title: 'Trump will take his dream to his grave': Iran says won't allow US warships in Hormuz
content: Iran has expressed its determination to prevent US military presence in the Persian Gulf amid escalating tensions. US Ambassador to Turkiye Tom Barrack mentioned the potential for a US strike on Iran this weekend. Despite threats, Barrack stated that President Trump continues to seek a diplomatic agreement. Trump emphasised that further military action remains a possibility if negotiations do not progress.

title: Did Van Gogh’s ‘Starry Night’ depict real sky from July 1889? Scientists think so
content: In a groundbreaking study, South Korean researchers have pinpointed July 22, 1889, as a possible date for the celestial scene depicted in The Starry Night. This new timeline disputes the widely accepted June 1889 date. The study notes that the alignment of stars aligns with observations from that evening, bolstered by van Gogh's letters that reference weather conditions, suggesting the artist's keen attention to his surroundings.

title: 'Four years, I never chased this jersey': Bhuvneshwar Kumar on India comeback
content: Bhuvneshwar Kumar credited patience, preparation and a no-expectations mindset for helping him return to international cricket after four years. The 36-year-old said the IPL and domestic cricket kept him sharp while improving his maturity. He also discussed modern T20 challenges, stressing that bowlers need smart strategies. India's strong start against New Zealand, he added, could boost confidence throughout the tour.

title: ‘Noise protest’ rocks Manipur valley districts, police fire tear gas
content: In a powerful display of unity, thousands of demonstrators took to the streets in various valley districts of Manipur, articulating their concerns over the escalating crisis. Using traditional means of noise-making, they called for urgent government intervention. Key demands included the establishment of the National Register of Citizens and an improved response to ethnic tensions, showcasing a strong public insistence for accountability and resolution.

title: Opposition's 'mock Parliament' to step up fight against SIR & CEC Gyanesh Kumar
content: Sources said a “mock” gathering depicting an assembly of MPs may take place in the national capital on Oct 28. The event will involve MPs and others, but is unlikely to be a large gathering, given that a massive show of strength to push for the CEC’s resignation is planned at Ramlila Maidan as a “Delhi chalo” rally.

title: 13k Pilibhit voter details changed, UP CEO calls it a ‘deliberate crime’
content: In a significant turn of events, an FIR has been filed against two SDMs and a voter registration operator due to allegations of fraudulent voter roll modifications. This manipulation has impacted more than 13,150 voters in the Pilibhit assembly constituency. The Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer emphasized the intentional nature of this act, calling it a crime rather than negligence.

title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
content: Mumbai Indians (MI) have roped in former Rajasthan Royals high-performance coach Steffan Jones as a bowling consultant for their development squad. Jones will work with MI's development squad alongside director of performance Zubin Bharucha, with the duo tasked with helping Indian players improve their skillsets.

title: Australian umpire's Ranji sojourn: Planes overhead at Palam, BKC's red soil pitch
content: Australian umpire Ben Treloar is experiencing Indian domestic cricket for the first time as part of the BCCI-Cricket Australia exchange programme. From aeroplanes flying overhead at Delhi's Palam ground to Mumbai's red-soil pitch at BKC, the 44-year-old shares his impressions of Indian first-class cricket, the warmth of its people and his growing love for local cuisine, including garlic naan and vada pav.

title: IND vs NZ: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in playing XI, but there's a twist
content: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl first against New Zealand in the second T20. The team made two changes, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi replacing Ishan Kishan and Prince Yadav coming in for Mayank Yadav. Iyer emphasized the importance of maintaining their aggressive approach while addressing fielding improvements. New Zealand also made a change, bringing in Jacob Duffy for Adam Milne.

title: Husband’s illicit relationship by itself is not cruelty: Madras high court
content: Madras high court ruled that a husband's illicit relationship is not sufficient for cruelty under Section 498A. This ruling came from a case involving a woman who committed suicide with her child. The court noted that more evidence is required to establish cruelty beyond mere allegations of an affair. The trial court had acquitted the husband due to insufficient evidence linking him to dowry harassment.

title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
content: US consumer sentiment has declined slightly as rising prices related to the Middle East conflict affect households' financial views. The Consumer Sentiment Index fell marginally to 48.0 in October, approaching a record low. Independents reported significantly weaker sentiment while Democrats and Republicans showed improvements. Inflation expectations rose, suggesting concerns about future price increases among consumers. The Federal Reserve is expected to maintain current interest rates during their upcoming meeting.

title: India script history with best-ever finish and record 114 medals at Asian Para Games
content: India concluded the Asian Para Games 2026 with an extraordinary display of talent, amassing a total of 114 medals, consisting of 30 gold, 35 silver, and 49 bronze. This achievement surpasses their previous record from 2022 edition, securing a commendable fourth place overall. The rise of India's para-athletes on the continental stage was evident, even as China led with an impressive 217 gold medals.

title: Woman medical officer assaulted, slapped and abused in police presence; video viral
content: A woman medical officer was assaulted and verbally abused by an accused during a medical examination. The accused was reportedly under the influence of alcohol when he attacked the doctor. Medical officers in Wardha district protested by boycotting work, highlighting safety concerns for healthcare personnel. Subsequently, police registered a case against the accused based on the medical officer's complaint.

title: As foam builds up in Yamuna, questions raised over how work was allotted
content: A defoaming operation is set to begin in Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj, with equipment already in place. The Aam Aadmi Party has raised concerns about the tender allocation process favoring a specific contractor. Allegations state that the contractor set up equipment before the bids were officially opened. Delhi Jal Board representatives clarify that they have conducted defoaming campaigns annually since 2022.

title: 11-year-old Indian-origin prodigy Bodhana breaks Polgar's 38-yo record
content: Eleven-year-old British chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandan has become the youngest female player to qualify for the International Master title, breaking Judit Polgar’s 38-year-old record. The English Chess Federation praised her as a “generational talent.” Already the youngest Woman Grandmaster qualifier, Bodhana has achieved several historic milestones and is now aiming to become a Grandmaster, chess’s highest title.

title: Watch: Paris shops increase security, board up windows, as France braces for protests
content: Shopkeepers in Paris are taking measures to secure their businesses against possible renewed protests and violence. Authorities are increasing police presence, with around 70,000 officers deployed this weekend across France. Demonstrations are planned in several cities, amidst ongoing political tensions leading to protests against rising living costs. While some support the protests, others condemn the associated looting and vandalism.

title: Mumbai Indians appoint Kieron Pollard as head coach ahead of IPL 2027
content: Kieron Pollard has been named the head coach of Mumbai Indians ahead of the IPL 2027 season. He takes over the position from Mahela Jayawardene, who has stepped down. Pollard expressed his gratitude for the opportunity and emphasised his connection to the team. The franchise is hopeful that Pollard will help restore their winning form. Mumbai Indians aims to build on their past successes and inspire their fans.

title: 18-year-old Anahat's historic run at Silicon Valley Open comes to an end
content: India’s Anahat Singh exited the Silicon Valley Open after losing 3-1 to Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam despite winning the opening game. Sivasangari praised the 18-year-old’s talent and potential after staging a comeback. Anahat had earlier defeated world No. 14 Salma Hany to become the first Indian woman since 2019 to reach a PSA Tour Gold-level semifinal.

title: 'Now is the time': Rubio warns Cuba next after Iran, asks Cubans to join hands
content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on Cubans to collaborate with intelligence agencies for positive change. He criticized the Cuban regime for corruption and unmet promises, suggesting this moment is crucial for action. The CIA later released a recruitment video encouraging Cubans to provide information discreetly. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump mentioned potential military actions nearby, heightening tensions over the situation.

title: Over 100 detained as SIR protests continue in Delhi
content: Hundreds of protesters including students and farmers gathered in Delhi to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They criticized the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls for resulting in unfair voter deletions. Many demonstrators were detained by police as tensions escalated during the protest. Demonstrations have been organized in 88 cities across 18 states involving numerous organizations.

title: Delhi HC junks Neha Bora plea against peace bond notice
content: The Delhi high court has denied AISA president Neha Bora's request to challenge a peace bond notice, which was raised amid concerns of potential peace disruption in a busy commercial district. The court determined that the special executive magistrate had enough evidence to issue the notice against Bora, who is facing several FIRs from the Delhi Police regarding public order violations.

title: 'PLA strong rival': MEA says China's patrolling deviations disturb border
content: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time. The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.

title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi gig gets police nod amid fresh threats
content: With security concerns arising, the Delhi Police initially refused to grant permission for Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert. Following constructive discussions with the organisers, improved safety protocols were established, including the addition of 1,500 personnel for crowd management. Attendees will be updated about transportation options in collaboration with cab providers. The concert is officially rescheduled for October 30 at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

title: Haryana power cut: Homes in dark for hours, residents block roads
content: A two-day power strike in Haryana caused significant disruptions across Gurgaon and surrounding areas. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini assured employees that no private power distribution licenses would be permitted. Outages led to water supply disruptions and industrial production halts, impacting many residents and businesses. Appeals were made by industry bodies for urgent government intervention to restore power.

title: ITBP Raising Day: PM Modi praises ‘Himveers’ as India-China border remains in focus
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other leaders extended their greetings to ITBP personnel on the occasion. They praised the courage and sacrifices made by the force in protecting India's borders. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh highlighted the contributions of ITBP towards internal security and border safeguarding. Meanwhile, the Indian Army and Home Minister Amit Shah also conveyed their regards.

title: US detains Bishnoi rival Himanshu Bhau after 4-yr manhunt, India may get custody soon
content: Himanshu Bhau, a notorious gangster from north India, was recently captured by the FBI in Las Vegas. He has been wanted for a series of violent offenses, including multiple murders and extortion schemes that have plagued Delhi and Haryana. After escaping juvenile detention in 2020, he maintained his criminal operations through illegal networks.

title: 15-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Telangana; 7 arrested
content: Seven individuals, including three minors, were arrested in Siddipet district for allegedly assaulting a 15-year-old girl. The incident occurred on Dasara when the victim's parents were away for agricultural work. The accused reportedly took the girl to a neighboring village and returned her the following morning. The victim identified the perpetrators, leading her father to file a police complaint.

title: When mob takes law into its own hands: another man lynched in Keralam’s Palakkad
content: The brutal lynching of an aurally challenged, unidentified man near the Moolathara dam in Keralam’s Palakkad has once again shaken the conscience of society. Abdul Latheef Naha speaks to investigators, psychiatrists and forensic experts to understand how did a homeless man become the target of a group that took it upon itself to punish him and such incidents are recurring.

title: In Adilabad, tribals find new sources of income from forests
content: From harvesting lac on Palash trees to making laddus from Mahua flowers, tribal communities in Adilabad are finding ways to earn more from forest resources they have relied on for generations. Supported by the district administration, the initiatives are helping families diversify their livelihoods while creating opportunities for tribal women to run small enterprises in their villages

title: Kolkata stampede: Death in the time of Durga Puja
content: On October 17, a stampede broke out at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, claiming 19 lives. The pandal, erected in a narrow space with dim lighting, was filled with people soon after it started raining. title: North Korea's Kim Jong-un makes surprise visit to China via newly opened bridge
content:
Kim Jong-un reportedly enters China via newly opened bridge

North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has reportedly made a surprise visit to China, arriving in the border city of Dandong through a newly opened bridge linking the two countries, Yonhap news agency reported on Saturday, citing a South Korean government source. Kim arrived in Dandong, in China's northeastern Liaoning province, via the New Yalu River Bridge, the source said. The visit would mark his first trip to China in more than a year. Earlier, reports suggested that strict traffic restrictions had been imposed in parts of Dandong. The New Yalu River Bridge, which connects North Korea's Sinuiju with China's Dandong, officially opened on October 15, more than a decade after its completion in 2014. The reported visit comes as US President Donald Trump seeks to resume dialogue with North Korea before the end of the year, ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.

End of Article
